output.question: Has General Motors announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. GM has cut jobs several times in 2026, but the newest report was not one I could confirm myself. Search results say GM Financial, GM's lending arm, cut about 400 jobs worldwide in early November 2026 'to support operating performance.' Both articles carrying that report (Automotive News and Auto Finance News) blocked access, so I could not read or confirm it. What I did confirm: on October 21, 2026, GM said it will close its Brownstown battery plant near Detroit when the lease runs out in summer 2027. The plant once had about 300 workers and now has fewer than a dozen. Before that, on May 11, 2026, GM laid off about 500 to 600 salaried staff, mostly IT roles in Austin, Texas, and Warren, Michigan, saying it was 'transforming its Information Technology organization.'

key_facts.fact: GM confirmed on October 21, 2026 that its Brownstown battery plant will close when its lease ends in summer 2027. The plant once had about 300 workers, fewer than a dozen remain, and GM is offering them other placements.
On May 11, 2026, GM laid off about 500 to 600 employees, mostly IT roles in Austin, Texas and Warren, Michigan. GM said it 'made the difficult decision to eliminate certain roles globally.'
Search results say GM Financial cut about 400 jobs worldwide in early November 2026. I could not open the article, so this is unconfirmed.

passages.quote: GM said it is "transforming its Information Technology organization to better position the company for the future" ... "made the difficult decision to eliminate certain roles globally."
GM confirmed the closure of its Brownstown battery plant south of Detroit on the same day it announced a $20 billion stock buyback

caveats: I could not open the GM Financial report of about 400 job cuts in November 2026 (both sites returned 403 errors). The number and date come only from search-result summaries. Also, GM Financial is GM's finance subsidiary, not the carmaker itself.
The Brownstown details come from the World Socialist Web Site, an openly left-wing outlet. It quotes GM's confirmation but not GM's own words, so I have no primary GM source for this.

Search results also mention other 2026 cuts I could not open and confirm: about 350 layoffs at GM's Lansing plants starting January 14, 2027 (Detroit News, August 14, 2026), about 1,100 jobs at Factory Zero in Detroit, and about 1,300 at Ultium Cells and Lordstown in Ohio in January 2026.
Factory-floor layoffs at GM are often described as temporary or tied to retooling a plant, and GM said its May IT cuts were not all permanent reductions in headcount.
